entries.german:
Cune v. Falkenstein (-kin-), Dompropst u. Vormund d. Mainzer Stifts, bekennt, daß d. Erzstift dem Ritter Conrad Rüdt (Rude), Burggraf zu Starkenburg (-kin-), nach der Abrechnung, die Cuno mit ihm vorgenommen hat, für Verluste, die er im Dienste des Erzbischofs von Mainz Heinrich III. von Virneburg, Cunos u. s. Mitvormünder erlitten hat, 1400 Pfd. H. Frankf. W. schuldet. Er versetzt ihm dafür mit Zust. d. Erzbischofs die Stadt Amorbach u. die Dörfer Schneeberg (Sneyt-), Buchen (Bu-), Weilbach (Wylen-), Reuental (Ruwen-), Buch, Kirchzell (Celle), Ottorfszell (Odolfcelle), Watterbach (-tenbuch) u. Dörnbach (Düring-) ohne die Fischerei, die H. Ebirhart v. Rosenberg von s. Amtes wegen innehat[a]. Amorbach bleibt M. offen. Den Schaden s. Diener hat Conrad noch nicht mitgerechnet, außer 50 Pfd. für einen Hengst des Conrad v. Neideck (Nydeke)[b] u. 35 Pfd. für einen Hengst des Rudolf v. Böckingen (Bekingin)[c] d. Ä. Geht A. in einem Krieg d. Erzbischofs verloren, so erhält Conrad sein Geld 1/4 Jahr darauf; wenn in eigener Sache, so hat er s. Geld, das Stift die Stadt verloren, falls sie nicht in einer Sühne zurückgegeben wird.

Siegler: Erzbischof, Cuno, Vormundsch. - D. geg. ist zu Eltevil 1350 uff den fritag vor sant Johannis Baptisten tag.[d] Fußnotenapparat: [a] s. Reg. 5820 (nr. 3). [b] OA. Öhringen? [c] OA. Heilbronn? [d] mit anderer Tinte von ders. Hand.
entries.abstract: Kuno II of Falkenstein, provost and guardian of the Mainz diocese, acknowledges that the diocese owes the knight Konrad Rüdt (Rude; von Collenberg), burgrave of Starkenburg (Starkinburg), according to the settlement Kuno II made with him, 1,400 pounds of Heller in Frankfurt currency for losses he suffered in the service of the Archbishop of Mainz, Heinrich III of Virneburg, Kuno, and his co-guardians. In return, with the archbishop's consent, he grants him the town of Amorbach and the villages of Schneeberg, Buchen, Weilbach, Reuental, Buch, Kirchzell, Ottorfszell, Watterbach, and Dörnbach, excluding the fishing rights held by Eberhard von Rosenberg by virtue of his office. Amorbach remains open to Mainz. Conrad has not yet counted the damages caused by his servants, except for 50 pounds for a stallion belonging to Conrad von Neideck and 35 pounds for a stallion belonging to Rudolf von Böckingen the Elder. If Amorbach is lost in a war waged by the archbishop, Conrad (Rüdt) receives his money a quarter of a year later. If Amorbach is lost in his own (Conrad's) cause, he loses his money (which he had lent to the archbishopric) and the city.
entries.english: Kuno von Falkenstein, provost and guardian of the Mainz church, acknowledges that the archbishopric owes the knight Konrad Rüdt, Burgrave of Starkenburg, 1,400 pounds Heller in Frankfurt currency for losses he suffered in the service of Archbishop Heinrich III of Virneburg of Mainz, Kuno, and their co-guardians. With the archbishop’s consent, he pledges the town of Amorbach and the villages of Schneeberg, Buchen, Weilbach, Reuental, Buch, Kirchzell, Ottorfszell, Watterbach, and Dörnbach, excluding the fishery held by Eberhard von Rosenberg by virtue of his office. Amorbach remains open to Mainz. The losses of Konrad’s servants are not yet included, except for 50 pounds for a stallion belonging to Konrad von Neideck and 35 pounds for a stallion belonging to Rudolf von Böckingen the Elder. If Amorbach is lost in a war of the archbishop, Konrad is to receive his money a quarter of a year later; if it is lost in his own cause, he loses both the money lent to the archbishopric and the town, unless the town is returned through a settlement. The archbishop, Kuno, and the guardians seal the document.
facts: Eberhard von Rosenberg holds fishery rights at Amorbach von Amtes wegen (by office)
